title: OpenAI settles DOJ allegation it shut US workers out of lucrative jobs
summary: OpenAI allegedly didn’t advertise certain jobs on its external website and or let U.S. workers apply online, according to the settlement.

title: KFF: Insurers want to hike small businesses’ premiums by 14% next year
summary: It’s becoming harder for small employers to offer insurance coverage, and another year of double-digit premium increases won’t help. Insurers say their hands are tied.

title: ADA may require reassignment despite worker’s inability to perform essential functions, 4th Circuit says
summary: The law’s "accommodation of last resort” has historically proven difficult for employers to administer.

title: Corporate conversations about AI productivity are mostly focused on future gains
summary: When it comes to the performance benefits of artificial intelligence, the vast majority of executives expect to realize results later on, a new report says.

title: July sees job losses, portending a potential rough patch for employers
summary: “Don’t put too much stock in a single report, but don’t ignore the fact that the plane is starting to shake,” a senior economist said.

title: Employers need to have conversations about menopause, experts say
summary: “First and foremost, we have to have a culture that fosters safety so that people feel safe to ask for the support that they need,” said Patty Borst from consultancy The Partners Group.

title: Must employers always wait before clarifying FMLA certifications with providers? Not necessarily, 4th Circuit says
summary: The ruling suggests employers don’t necessarily have to wait for workers to fix authenticity problems with Family and Medical Leave Act certification documents.

title: Wage compression — not job cuts — may be the outcome of AI adoption at work
summary: Employers may have to square cost savings with a workforce that is less financially secure.

title: Gen X employees say they are burned out from caregiving responsibilities
summary: Caregiving demands “inevitably spill over to the workday,” yet a third of employees reported receiving little or no support from their employer.

title: Payscale: Merit increases remain popular as ‘peanut butter’ raises trend downward
summary: In the U.S., 30% of employers said they expect salary budgets to be higher year over year in 2027, up substantially from 16% reported last year.
